items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The night before, there was a boxing match between Joe Louis and Max Baer and I took the risk to come over to New York that night and celebrate Joe's victory in a bar on 7th Avenue and 143rd Street after hearing the fight on the radio.

ctx.x: I had to come to the big city for my passport and before going downtown, I was sitting in Freddy's car on 138th street between Lenox and 5th Avenue when I saw a musician that I knew coming down the street. I ducked down in the car like a criminal that was being hunted by the law because I could not afford to have my plans go wrong at that stage of the game.

I was to leave on the French Line's Normandy, the 25th of September and it was decided between Beezie and I that I would send for her after I had been in Paris one month. The night before, there was a boxing match between Joe Louis and Max Baer and I took the risk to come over to New York that night and celebrate Joe's victory in a bar on 7th Avenue and 143rd Street after hearing the fight on the radio. Harlem was jumping but I didn't run into anyone that I knew, and it would not have mattered much that night…

I think the sailing time for the "Normandie" was 10 a.m. and I had to see my buddy Dick Wells before I left. I have not even written him from Cincinnati to let him know that I was going to Europe although I was certain that he would have kept it a secret if I had asked him. But I just wasn't taking any chances. So we came from Leonia early in the morning of the 25th and I woke Dickie up about 8 and told him what was happening. He was real happy to see me. I told him why I had left New York which he did not know…
